title: National Housing Finance and Investment Corporation Bill 2018
short_title: National Housing Finance and Investment Corporation Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill is part of a package that would create the National Housing Finance and Investment Corporation to help Australians access better housing.
The corporation would run a $1 billion fund for housing infrastructure and an aggregator to lower financing costs for community housing providers.
The bill requires a review of the corporation's operations three years after it starts.
changes: Establishes the National Housing Finance and Investment Corporation as a corporate Commonwealth entity.
Creates a $1 billion National Housing Infrastructure Facility to finance infrastructure for housing supply.
Sets up an Affordable Housing Bond Aggregator to improve financing efficiency for community housing providers.
Requires a review of the primary bill's operation three years after commencement.
summary.affected: Australians, community housing providers, and organisations that provide subsidised housing for low-income people.

speeches.speaker: Michael Sukkar
speeches.brief: The National Housing Finance and Investment Corporation Bill 2018 establishes the NHFIC to improve housing outcomes, particularly for vulnerable Australians, by administering a $1 billion National Housing Infrastructure Facility and an affordable housing bond aggregator, with an independent board and a legislative guarantee. The government also announced a new National Housing and Homelessness Agreement with indexed and permanent homelessness funding.

speeches.speaker: Michael Sukkar
speeches.brief: The bill amends the Administrative Decisions (Judicial Review) Act and the Freedom of Information Act to exempt the National Housing Finance and Investment Corporation from providing reasons for decisions and disclosing commercial documents, consistent with exemptions for bodies like the Export Finance and Insurance Corporation, NBN Co, and Indigenous Business Australia. It also includes transitional provisions to allow the corporation to begin its core lending, investment and grant functions from 1 July 2018.

speeches.speaker: Julian Leeser
speeches.brief: The National Housing Finance and Investment Corporation Bill 2018 establishes an independent entity to administer an affordable housing bond aggregator and a $1 billion National Housing Infrastructure Facility, aiming to improve housing affordability. The speaker also highlighted government measures including the First Home Super Saver Scheme and downsizing incentives, and criticised Labor's proposed removal of negative gearing and capital gains tax increases.

speeches.speaker: Tony Zappia
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that housing affordability has declined due to state government disinvestment in public housing, closure of public banks, upfront infrastructure charges, negative gearing and capital gains tax concessions costing $12 billion annually, and foreign buyers. They criticised the $1 billion fund as a paltry slush fund with unclear conditions, potential for pork-barrelling, and no guarantee of cheaper housing, and opposed using superannuation for housing.

speeches.speaker: Emma Husar
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that Labor first proposed a bond aggregator for affordable housing a year ago, criticised the Liberal government's housing policies as inadequate and out of touch, and highlighted specific concerns that the National Housing Finance and Investment Corporation board lacks diversity and transparency, noting it will not be subject to the Freedom of Information Act. The speaker also cited the International Monetary Fund’s endorsement of Labor’s proposed reforms to negative gearing and capital gains tax, and stated Labor will not oppose the bill but will refer it to a Senate inquiry.

speeches.speaker: Michael Sukkar
speeches.brief: The National Housing Finance and Investment Corporation Bill 2018 establishes an independent corporate entity to administer a $1 billion National Housing Infrastructure Facility and an affordable housing bond aggregator, aiming to boost housing supply, improve affordability for first home buyers and low-to-middle-income Australians, and enhance social housing outcomes. The speaker noted that housing supply has not kept up with demand, particularly in major cities, and cited figures including $7.6 billion in Commonwealth housing expenditure in 2016-17, 40,000 on community housing waiting lists, and 148,000 on public housing waiting lists.
